A bubble chart is not a specific kind of pie chart. Pie charts encode parts-of-a-whole as area proportions of a circle; bubble charts encode data points as circles whose radius/area maps to a value but do not necessarily sum to a whole. Bubble charts show multidimensional data (x, y, size) — more like a scatter plot with an encoded size channel. A competent speaker would not call a bubble chart 'a pie chart.' This is an INSTANCE_OF error against the wrong target (and the note itself mischaracterizes what a bubble chart does).

INSTANCE_OF requires filing against the nearest kind. 'Tool' is too broad — vaccines are more specifically medical interventions, biologics, or pharmaceuticals. Clearly human-made: a software construct for temporary data holding and transfer via cut-copy-paste. Scope correctly carves the concept, not any particular implementation. Valid entry under Law 1.

Definition carves the concept: states what a clipboard is (temporary holding area), its parameters (text/images/files), and persistence mechanism (virtual buffer in OS/application). Ends with proper Law 6 trailer. Law 4 satisfied.

Removal test passes: remove user-interface and the clipboard loses its domain entirely — it mediates data transfer between application and UI, with no operation outside a UI context. The construct is defined by its UI-mediated clipboard workflow.

Skeuomorphism is designed for the sake of user interfaces — it provides familiar visual cues that help users understand digital systems. The servant (skeuomorphism) points at the master (user-interface). This is a clean SERVES claim: purpose by design, not mere incidental benefit.

DEPENDS_ON fails: skeuomorphism is visual resemblance to real-world counterparts, but it does not NEED metaphor to operate now. Visual design can evoke real-world analogues without invoking conceptual metaphor as an active mechanism. The note conflates thematic inspiration with constitutive dependency. This is better captured by SERVES (to UI) or INSTANCE_OF (of design technique).
Clipboard is a well-defined software construct: a virtual buffer for temporary data holding and transfer in cut-copy-paste workflows. Clearly human-made, scope is precise and on the made side.

Definition accurately describes clipboard as a temporary holding area for data, operating as a virtual buffer in the OS. Carves the parameters (temporary, virtual buffer, data types covered) and persistence mechanism (OS-level software construct). Legal trailer present.

Experience is knowledge acquired through direct participation rather than abstract study. A competent speaker would recognize experience as a kind of knowledge ('learned by experience', 'practical experience taught me'). The removal test isn't needed for INSTANCE_OF — the question is whether experience is a specific case of knowledge, and it clearly is: knowledge has multiple acquisition modes (observation, testimony, participation), and experience is participation-based knowledge.

Skeuomorphism is designed and maintained to serve user interfaces — it provides familiar real-world cues that help users understand digital systems. The servant (skeuomorphism) points at the master (user-interface). This is a textbook SERVES: the purpose of skeuomorphism is to further the operation of the UI by making it more intuitive.

The removal test fails: clipboards operate fully in CLI environments (pbcopy/pbpaste on macOS, xclip/xsel on Linux, tmux paste buffers) without any graphical user interface. The clipboard is a data-transfer mechanism, not a UI construct. Its core function (temporary holding and transfer of data) operates independently of any interface modality.

Skeuomorphism is about visual/design resemblance to real-world objects (e.g., a trash can icon, a notepad app with lined paper). Conceptual metaphor is a cognitive mechanism mapping from one domain to another. Skeuomorphism operates through surface-level visual analogy, not conceptual structure. Remove metaphor as a cognitive mechanism and skeuomorphism still works as a design technique — it just becomes literal ornamentation. The removal test fails.

Experience is not a specific kind of knowledge — it is a process or source of acquiring knowledge. A competent speaker would not say 'experience is a form of knowledge' but rather 'experience provides knowledge.' The INSTANCE_OF test fails: experience is the pathway, knowledge is the output. Law 9a: a thing is not an instance of what it produces.

Skeuomorphism does not depend on metaphor. The removal test: remove metaphor and skeuomorphism still operates — it works through visual/functional resemblance, not conceptual metaphor. A skeuomorphic button looks like a physical button via shape/shadow/texture, not via metaphor. This confuses the mechanism (resemblance) with a different concept (metaphor). Law 8b: 'constitutive' without showing removal's consequence carries no weight.

Skeuomorphism SERVES user-interface: it is a design technique deliberately maintained for the sake of user interfaces, providing familiar visual cues. The servant (skeuomorphism) points at the master (user-interface). This is a clean SERVES — by design, not incidental benefit. Law 8d satisfied.

The clipboard does not DEPEND_ON user-interface. The removal test: remove UI and the clipboard still operates as a system-level data transfer mechanism (CLI copy/paste, drag-drop without visible UI, programmatic clipboard access). The clipboard's mechanism is memory allocation and data formats, not UI mediation. Law 8b: the note says 'clipboard stops operating entirely' without UI, but that is false — the clipboard works at the OS level.
Clipboard is clearly human-made: a software construct for temporary data holding. Scope correctly identifies it as a virtual buffer for cut-copy-paste workflows. Law 1 satisfied.

Definition correctly carves clipboard: states parameters (temporary holding area for data), persistence mechanism (virtual buffer in OS or application), and the operational scope (cut/copy/paste workflows). Law 4 satisfied. Trailer: [formal: clipboard | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01] — appropriate for a software construct.

Experience is a SOURCE or PROCESS of gaining knowledge, not a KIND of knowledge. Per Law 9a, INSTANCE_OF asks whether a competent speaker would call X 'a Y'. No competent speaker says 'experience is a kind of knowledge' — they distinguish 'gaining knowledge through experience' from 'having knowledge'. Experience is participation and exposure; knowledge is the resulting understanding. Conflating source with product violates the nearest-kind requirement (Law 11e). The correct edge might be experience DERIVED_FROM participation or experience SERVES learning, but not INSTANCE_OF knowledge.

Fails the removal test (Law 8b): skeuomorphism as a design technique — making digital elements resemble real-world counterparts — does not stop operating if the concept of metaphor is removed. The note conflates the mechanism (visual resemblance) with a theoretical explanation (conceptual metaphor). This is meta-level, not object-level dependency.

Clear SERVES relation per Law 8d. Skeuomorphism is designed and maintained for the sake of user interfaces — the servant (skeuomorphism) points at the master (user-interface). Its purpose is to provide familiar visual cues for UI understanding.

Experience is a SOURCE of knowledge, not a KIND of knowledge. Per Law 9a: INSTANCE_OF asks whether a competent speaker would call X 'a Y'. No competent speaker calls experience 'a knowledge.' Experience is direct involvement; knowledge is a state of knowing. The relation is causal/epistemic (experience yields knowledge), not hierarchical.

Clear made-side entry: a pointed human-made instrument for writing, drawing, or screen interaction. Has specific parameters (pointed, hand-held, instrument) and persistence mechanism (physical tool used in writing/drawing practices). Law 3a confirms even specific instruments are fileable. Well-scoped.

Experience is not a kind of knowledge — it is participation, exposure, or engagement itself. The note conflates the source of knowledge with knowledge itself: 'knowledge gained through direct involvement' describes how experience PRODUCES knowledge, not that experience IS knowledge. A competent speaker would not call experience 'a knowledge'; they would call it a means of gaining it. This files nothing under INSTANCE_OF.

Sublimation channels impulses into socially acceptable outlets — but expression is only ONE possible outlet among many (work, art, sport, science). The PRIMARY purpose is tension resolution and social adaptation, not expression. The note over-specifies the target: 'for the sake of expression' is too narrow for what sublimation actually serves. It might SERVES emotional regulation or social adaptation, but expression is incidental rather than constitutive of its purpose.

Clear, well-carved scope for a human-made instrument. Specifies form (pointed), function (writing/drawing/touch interaction), and substrate (matter). Distinguishes from related tools (pen, pencil) by its interaction surface range including capacitive screens.

Well-carved definition: three clear parameters (pointed form, application of marks, precision over finger), substrate is matter, lists concrete surfaces. Trailer is present and appropriate. The definition would not fit many things (distinguishes from pens/pencils by touch-surface interaction) and fits this thing precisely.

sublimation is built for the sake of expression: it channels unacceptable impulses into socially acceptable or productive outlets. Per Law 8d, the designed purpose is to produce expression — the servant (sublimation) points at the master (expression).
Clear scope: a pointed instrument for writing, drawing, or touch interaction. Human-made, extends hand precision. Passes Law 1 (made side) and Law 2a (map of the instrument, not any physical stylus).

Well-carved definition: parameters (pointed, hand-held, precision over finger), persistence (physical manufacture + practice of use). Correctly identifies substrate as mind+behavior and trailer is complete.

clipboard IS a specific kind of tool: a passive artifact that extends human capacity to hold or temporarily store content for later retrieval. Per Law 11c, shelves/jars/walls qualify as tools; clipboard is the same category — an artifact extending a human capacity. The filer pinned the correct sense (tool as artifact extending capacity). Law 11e ladder check: clipboard is not already INSTANCE_OF tool via intermediate rung.

The removal test is correctly applied here, not the which-came-first test. A MacBook Air as a functional computer concept cannot operate without an operating system — remove the OS concept and the hardware cannot run software, manage resources, or serve as a computing device. This is a real operational dependency (Law 8), not a meta-level claim about naming/sayability (Law 2b). The MB Air hardware alone is just metal and silicon; its identity as a functioning computer is constituted by its dependency on an OS.

The note mischaracterizes sublimation. In psychoanalytic theory, sublimation is a defense mechanism — an automatic psychological process, not something 'built or maintained for the sake of' anything. Law 8d requires a designed purpose or sustained practice. Sublimation may result in expression as a side effect, but it is not designed for expression. The SERVES relation requires intent or sustained practice as a means; this conflates outcome with purpose. A better edge might be DERIVED_FROM (psychoanalytic theory DERIVED_FROM expression studies) or no edge at all.

Stylus fits Law 1 perfectly — it is a human-made pointed instrument for writing/drawing/interacting with touch surfaces. The scope correctly avoids claiming natural territory (pressure, touch sensation) and focuses on the constructed artifact. The definition carves well: pointed, hand-held, designed for precision interaction — distinguishes it from pen (ink-delivery), finger (body part), and stylus-like tools (e.g., chopsticks). ScopeJustification is solid.

Definition properly carves: states parameters (pointed, hand-held, precision over finger) and persistence (physical or digital instantiation). The trailer format is correct. Distinguishes stylus from pen (no ink), finger (precision), and generic tool (specific interaction mode). Law 4 parameters present; Law 6 trailer present.

clipboard is a passive artifact that extends human capacity for temporary storage and retrieval — a tool in the broad kingdom sense. Per Law 11c, passive artifacts (shelves, jars, walls, clipboards) qualify exactly as active implements do.

The removal test asks: does the MacBook Air stop OPERATING without the OS concept? The hardware can still boot into recovery mode, run firmware, and perform diagnostics. It may be crippled for practical use but does not cease to operate entirely. The argument conflates intended function with operational capacity.

Per Law 8d, SERVES requires that X is built or maintained for the sake of Y. In psychoanalytic theory, sublimation's purpose is impulse transformation and defense — redirecting unacceptable urges. Artistic or social expression may be an incidental byproduct, not the designed purpose. The note asserts purpose without showing design intent.

Good definition that carves: pointed instrument, applied to surface, precision over finger. Parameters are specific (shape, material, interaction model), persistence mechanism is clear (tool design across physical and digital forms). Trailer complete. Would fit only a stylus and no other instrument.

A clipboard is a specific kind of tool: an artifact (physical or digital) that extends human capacity to temporarily hold and retrieve content. A competent speaker would say 'a clipboard is a tool' — it is a kind of artifact that extends a human capacity, which is the kingdom's definition of tool (Law 11c). Per Law 9, specific→general.

The removal test fails at the object level. A MacBook Air is a line of laptop computers — its concept includes hardware designed to run an OS, but the concept of a laptop/computer does not depend on the concept of an operating system. A computing device that requires specific software to boot is better expressed as INSTANCE_OF (it is a kind of computer that needs an OS), or as DEPENDS_ON on a specific OS, not on the broad category. The note conflates a product's design specification with an object-level dependency: the concept of operating system is a general class of software; the MacBook Air depends on running some OS, not on the abstract concept itself.

A stylus IS a specific kind of tool: a physical or digital writing implement that extends the human capacity to mark surfaces. A competent speaker would call it a tool. Per Law 11c, passive artifacts qualify as tools.

A clipboard IS a specific kind of tool: a physical or digital artifact that extends human capacity to hold and transport content for later use. A competent speaker would call a clipboard a tool. Per Law 11c, passive artifacts (shelves, jars, walls, clipboards) qualify as tools.

This conflates practical coupling with constitutive dependency. A MacBook Air is designed to run a specific OS, but the removal test asks: remove 'operating-system' as a concept entirely — does the MacBook Air stop operating? A computer could run bare-metal firmware or embedded code without an operating system as a category. The edge mistakes implementation detail for conceptual dependency. A better edge would be macbook air DEPENDS_ON firmware (more constitutive) or macbook air DERIVED_FROM personal-computer (historical).

wireframe IS a kind of prototype: a low-fidelity structural representation of layout/structure before visual design. A competent speaker would call a wireframe 'a type of prototype.' The removal test is not at issue here — this is INSTANCE_OF, not DEPENDS_ON. Direction is correct.

metronome SERVES cadence: a metronome's designed purpose is to produce and sustain a steady rhythmic pulse. Per Law 8d, the servant (metronome) points at the master (cadence). This is teleological, not dependency — correct edge type.

stylus IS a specific kind of tool: a writing implement that extends human capacity to make marks or interact with surfaces. Per Law 11c, passive artifacts (shelves, jars, walls) qualify as tools. A competent speaker would call a stylus 'a tool.' Direction is correct.
wireframe entry scope is clearly human-made: a design artifact for digital interfaces. Well-defined, on the made side.

wireframe definition carves: low-fidelity visual schematic, parameters are omission of color/typography/imagery, persistence is through design practice and communication. Needs the Law 6 trailer but the definition itself is substantive.

Anchoring effect and Dunning-Kruger effect are two distinct cognitive biases, not a specific→general relationship. Both are kinds of cognitive bias, so INSTANCE_OF between them is structurally wrong per Law 9. They might share a DEPENDS_ON edge or be related via some other mechanism, but one is NOT a subtype of the other.

A wireframe IS a low-fidelity prototype — specifically, a structural/layout prototype without visual design. A competent speaker would say 'a wireframe is a type of prototype.' Prototype is the nearest kind. Per Law 9 and 9a, this is a correct INSTANCE_OF.

A metronome is built and maintained for the sake of cadence — its designed purpose is to produce and sustain a steady rhythmic pulse. Per Law 8d (SERVES), the servant points at the master. This correctly files teleology, not dependency.

Knowledge DEPENDS_ON experience fails Law 2b and the removal test. 'Without lived experience to draw from, the concept of accumulated understanding has nothing to accumulate' argues at the meta-level — that knowledge as a CONCEPT needs experience to exist. Per Law 2b, the map's shadow (every concept needs cognition/language) files nothing. At the object level, knowledge as a construct can be transmitted via teaching, books, and language without the knower having direct experience. The removal test: remove individual experience — does the concept of knowledge cease to OPERATE? No, because knowledge can still be accumulated second-hand through testimony and instruction.

A stylus IS a specific kind of tool — a writing implement that extends human capacity to make marks or interact with touch surfaces. Per Law 11c, passive artifacts (shelves, jars, walls) qualify as tools. A competent speaker would call a stylus 'a type of tool.' The nearest kind is tool.

Scope is clear and on the made side: wireframe is a human-made artifact of software design. The scope correctly describes it as 'a low-fidelity visual guide depicting the skeletal layout of a digital interface' — this is a well-carved scope that places it on the made side.

The definition correctly carves wireframe with parameters: (1) low-fidelity, (2) structural layout focus, (3) deliberate omission of visual design. The persistence mechanism (subtype documentation practice in software design) is stated. Law 4 compliance is good. The trailer is properly formatted.

Dunning-Kruger is a specific cognitive bias (overestimation due to low ability). Anchoring is a different cognitive bias (insufficient adjustment from an initial value). One is not a kind of the other — they are parallel instances. The note itself admits 'these are two different biases, not a general-specific relationship.' STRIKE.

Knowledge as a concept does not stop operating if you remove experience — it stops being SAYABLE, which is a meta-level loss per Law 2b. The removal test of Law 8 asks whether X stops OPERATING, not whether it stops being nameable. Formal logic, mathematics, and many domains of knowledge can be operated as concepts without personal experience. 'Constitutive' asserted without showing the removal's consequence carries no weight per Law 8b.

A wireframe IS a specific kind of prototype — specifically a low-fidelity structural one. Per Law 9, a competent speaker would call a wireframe 'a type of prototype.' Prototype is the nearest kind. The note correctly identifies the relationship.

A metronome is built and maintained for the sake of cadence — its designed purpose is to produce and sustain a steady rhythmic pulse. Per Law 8d (SERVES), the servant (metronome) points at the master (cadence). The note correctly applies the teleology test.

A stylus IS a specific kind of tool — a writing implement that extends human capacity to make marks or interact with touch surfaces. Per Law 11c, passive artifacts qualify as tools (broad sense: any artifact extending human capacity). Per Law 11e, tool is the nearest kind — no intermediate rung. The note correctly cites Law 11c.

Well-crafted scope: clearly states the entry is human-made (a design artifact), defines its purpose (communicate structural hierarchy before visual design), and its parameters (low-fidelity, skeletal layout). The scope correctly frames it as a construct, not a natural thing. Fits Law 1.

Definition correctly carves the concept: parameters are clear (low-fidelity, structural, omits decoration), persistence mechanism identified (design documentation / team communication). The definition stays at the object level (what wireframes do) rather than meta-level. Includes proper Law 6 trailer.

Anchoring-effect and dunning-kruger-effect are two distinct cognitive biases, not a specific→general relationship. One is not a kind of the other — both would be INSTANCE_OF cognitive-bias. The filer's own note admits this should not be INSTANCE_OF.

The note says without lived experience the concept has nothing to accumulate. Per Law 2b this is a meta-level claim — true of every entry, files nothing. Per Law 8b the removal test asks whether X stops OPERATING, not whether it stops being SAYABLE. Knowledge as a concept can still operate as a category without experience.

A wireframe is a low-fidelity visual guide for layout; a prototype is a functional model for testing. They are parallel artifacts in the design process, not specific→general. A competent speaker would not say a wireframe is a type of prototype — wireframes show structure, prototypes show function.

Classic purpose/teleology: a metronome is built and maintained for the sake of cadence — its sole designed purpose is to produce and sustain a steady rhythmic pulse. Per Law 8d, the servant (metronome) points at the master (cadence). This is SERVES, not DEPENDS_ON.
Well-scoped: a low-fidelity visual guide for skeletal layout. Clearly human-made (Law 1), clearly a map not territory (Law 2a). The scope justifies what it is and why it persists.
Definition carves: specifies low-fidelity, omits color/typography/imagery, maps structural layout. Has a proper trailer with form, substrate, horizon, explicit, and epoch. Meets Law 4 and Law 6.

The note argues knowledge needs 'lived experience' to accumulate — that is territory, not map. Per Law 2b, knowledge as a concept does not depend on actual lived experience; it depends on the concept of experience. The removal test fails at the object level: remove lived experience and the concept of knowledge still operates. This is a meta-level dependency that files nothing per Law 2b.

The note admits anchoring-effect and dunning-kruger-effect are 'two different biases' — they cannot be in a general-specific (INSTANCE_OF) relationship. Both are cognitive biases; neither is a kind of the other. Filed against the wrong target entirely.
Clear human-made interface construct. Scope specifies reversibility of recent actions via a stack of operations. Fits Law 1 and Law 2 with a well-defined carve.

Definition properly carves: temporal locality (operates on immediate past), stack-based implementation (LIFO), and reversibility (undoes most recent action). Has a clear Law 6 trailer. Maps the concept without drifting into territory.

Undo is a well-scoped interface construct: reversibility via a stack of operations. The scope correctly identifies it as human-made (software UI construct) with a clear persistence mechanism (stack). The removal test passes — without undo, many applications lose their core error-recovery mechanism.
Definition properly carves undo with parameters (temporal locality, stack of operations) and persistence mechanism. The definition targets the concept, not the feeling of reversal. Trailer present.
Clear scope: undo is a human-made interface construct providing reversibility via operation stack. Well-carved parameters.
Definition properly carves: temporal locality + stack of operations. Ends with valid trailer. Maps to the interface construct described in the entry.

Undo is clearly human-made — a software interface construct implementing reversibility via operation stacks. The scope clearly states it's built to persist across software applications. Law 1 satisfied.

The definition is thin on parameters and persistence mechanism (Law 4). It describes a UI operation but lacks proper boundaries. More critically, it's missing the mandatory Law 6 trailer at the end. A competent definition would explain stack semantics, reversal limits, and the persistence mechanism across applications.

A cadenza is NOT a kind of performance (Law 9a). A cadenza is a compositional element — a written solo passage within a musical work. A performance is the act of presenting music. Confusing a part with its presentation category. A competent speaker would not call a cadenza 'a kind of performance' — they'd call it a passage, section, or musical element.

A cadenza is a structural passage within a musical composition — it is a part of a performance, not a kind of performance itself. INSTANCE_OF requires that a competent speaker calls X a kind of Y. One would not call a cadenza 'a performance'; one would call it a passage, section, or element of a performance. The correct relation, if any, is CONTAINS (performance CONTAINS cadenza) or structural/part-of, not INSTANCE_OF.

A tradition is a specific kind of practice — a behavior, belief, or custom transmitted across generations. A competent speaker would readily say 'a tradition is a kind of practice.' The note pins the operative sense clearly, and INSTANCE_OF files against the nearest kind without leaping.

A cadenza is a solo passage WITHIN a performance, not a performance itself. A competent speaker would say 'a cadenza is a musical passage' or 'a performance section,' not 'a kind of performance.' The nearest kind is not 'performance' — that's a whole event type. This is a leap to a too-broad target.

A ritual IS a kind of praxis (practice). Ritual = structured sequence of symbolic actions performed with intention and repetition. A competent speaker readily calls a ritual 'a kind of practice.' The sense is clear and the nearest-kind mapping is sound.

A tradition IS a kind of practice. Tradition = behavior/belief/custom maintained across generations through deliberate transmission. A competent speaker would call a tradition 'a kind of practice.' Clear INSTANCE_OF against the nearest kind.

A cadenza IS a kind of performance. It is a solo passage in music where the performer displays mastery — clearly a specific type of performance. The nearest-kind mapping is correct and a competent speaker would say 'a cadenza is a performance.'

Ritual is a specific kind of practice: a structured, repeated sequence of actions performed with symbolic intent. A competent speaker would call a ritual 'a kind of praxis' (engaged, patterned activity). The INSTANCE_OF direction is correct — ritual is the specific, praxis is the general kind.

Tradition is a specific kind of practice: a behavior, belief, or custom maintained across generations. A competent speaker would call a tradition 'a kind of practice.' The direction tradition→practice is correct for INSTANCE_OF.

A ritual is a specific kind of practice — a structured sequence of actions performed with symbolic intent, maintained through repetition and social transmission. Clean INSTANCE_OF: ritual is a type of praxis (structured practice), and a competent speaker would call a ritual 'a kind of practice.' No meta-level fluff, no identity/purpose confusion.

Tradition is a specific kind of practice — behavior, belief, or custom transmitted across generations. Clean INSTANCE_OF: tradition is a subtype of practice, and a competent speaker would call a tradition 'a practice.' The note pins a clear sense. No ladder issue — practice is the nearest kind.

Cant is NOT a poetic meter. In English, cant means: (1) a sloped surface, (2) specialized jargon of a group, (3) insincere religious language. The note conflates cant with chant. No English sense of 'cant' matches 'poetic meter.'

Experience depends on memory is meta-level per Law 2b: the concept of experience, like every concept, requires cognition/memory to be held, but that doesn't file an object-level edge between the entries. The note argues the concept's content rather than showing an operational dependency.

Distraction is not a kind of attention — it is the misdirection or failure of attention. A competent speaker would not call distraction 'a form of attention.' It relates TO attention but is not a subtype, so INSTANCE_OF is wrong.

A ritual IS a kind of praxis. Praxis = purposeful, practice-based action. A ritual is a structured sequence of actions performed with symbolic intent, maintained through repetition. A competent speaker would call a ritual 'a form of praxis' or 'a kind of practice.' The note pins the sense of praxis as structured, repeated action with intent — and ritual fits perfectly.

Sublimation's designed purpose is psychological regulation — channeling unacceptable impulses into socially acceptable ones (Freudian defense mechanism). Expression is an incidental byproduct, not the designed purpose. The note confuses benefit with teleology. Law 8d requires the purpose to be 'built or maintained for the sake of' the target.

The note correctly distinguishes meta-level from object-level. Undo as a mechanism operates on stored states — remove the concept of storing/recalling past states and the mechanism ceases to function. This is not just about sayability; the entire operational structure collapses without it. Object-level dependency confirmed.

Functional fixedness is not about perception as a general faculty — it is a cognitive bias that misapplies past experience to perception. The removal test fails: remove general perception (the capacity to see objects), and functional fixedness cannot operate at all. But the bias itself is a pattern of memory/learning overriding perception, not a dependency on perception. A better edge would be INSTANCE_OF cognitive-bias.

Cant as specialized jargon (the more common meaning) is not a kind of meter — it is a register of language. The note conflates the narrow poetic meaning with a broader concept. Even in classical poetry, 'cant' refers to a melodic chanting style rather than a metrical pattern. A competent speaker would not describe cant as 'a meter.'

The note correctly pins object-level: the concept of 'lived experience' is defined by accumulation and recall of events — its operational mechanism requires the memory function. Remove memory as a stored/recall mechanism and the concept of accumulated experience collapses. Not merely sayability but the concept's structure depends on memory.

The pinned sense is distraction as 'attention directed away from its intended focus.' A competent speaker would describe distraction as 'a form of attention' or 'attention gone astray' — the filer's framing matches. INSTANCE_OF is correct: distraction is a specific case of the broader attention faculty.

Vernacular is the everyday speech of a community, and it is built and maintained for the sake of communication within that group. The removal test: remove communication and vernacular — a tool for intra-group communication — has no purpose. This is a genuine SERVES relationship: the designed purpose of vernacular is to further communication. The note correctly pins the teleological direction: servant (vernacular) → master (communication).

Cant is NOT a kind of meter. The primary meaning of 'cant' is specialized jargon or argot of a group — and in no recognized poetic tradition is 'cant' a meter type. The note conflates it with 'canzone' (a poetic form) or misstates what 'cant' means. 'Cant' is not a rhythmic pattern or poetic meter, so 'cant INSTANCE_OF meter' fails the competent-speaker test: no competent speaker would say 'cant is a kind of meter.'

Distraction is not a kind of attention — it is a phenomenon OF attention, not a kind OF it. The correct relation would be DEPENDS_ON (distraction needs attention to exist) or CONTAINS (distraction involves attentional processes), but INSTANCE_OF fails the competent-speaker test: no one would say 'distraction is a type of attention.' Distraction is attention misdirected or diverted, not a subclass of attention.

Experience as a human-made concept (the map) is defined by the accumulation and recall of events — its operating mechanism IS memory. Remove the concept of memory (storing and recalling past states) and the concept of lived experience loses its mechanism entirely: without memory there can be no 'accumulation' or 'recall.' This is object-level, not meta: the concept of experience literally operates through the faculty of memory, not merely through language/naming.

Undo operates by storing prior states and later recalling them to reverse. Remove the concept of memory (storing/recalling past states) and undo cannot function — it has no mechanism. This is object-level: undo literally operates through memory. The removal test passes — undo stops operating without memory.

Functional fixedness is a cognitive bias about categorization and mental sets — the tendency to see objects only in their conventional roles. The removal test fails: remove the concept of perception and the bias (misapplying past experience to problem-solving) still operates. It targets categorization, not the perception faculty itself.

Sublimation is a psychological defense mechanism that redirects unacceptable impulses into socially acceptable outlets. The note claims its designed purpose is to further expression — but sublimation's purpose is emotional/psychological regulation and social functioning, NOT expression. Expression may be the output, but it's not the purpose. 'For whose sake?' The answer is the individual's psychological balance and social integration. The filer confuses result with purpose: sublimation produces art (expression), but it serves the psyche, not expression.
An initialism (e.g. FBI, NASA) is a specific type of abbreviation formed from initial letters. The competent-speaker test passes.

Sublimation is a psychoanalytic defense mechanism — it channels impulses into productive outlets. But it is not built or maintained for the sake of expression per Law 8d: it is an automatic psychological process, not a tool or practice designed for expression. Expression is its output, not its designed purpose.

Undo stores prior states and reverses to them. Remove memory (capacity to store and recall past states) and undo has no mechanism to operate. This is object-level: undo's own mechanism is memory-based storage. Law 8 removal test passes.

Functional fixedness locks perception of an object's function to its conventional use. Remove perception and functional fixedness cannot operate. Unlike cognitive-affordance (which IS perception, identity not dependency), functional fixedness operates THROUGH perception as a bias. Law 8 removal test passes.

Cant is not a recognized poetic meter. Cant means specialized jargon/hypocritical language or a slanted angle. The filer invents a sense of cant as a rhythmic pattern — not a standard or attested meter. The competent-speaker test fails.

The concept of experience is defined by accumulated remembered events — memory is constitutive of the concept's content. Remove memory and lived experience as a concept collapses. Object-level dependency, not meta-level.

Distraction is not a type of attention — it is attention misdirected or captured involuntarily. A competent speaker would not say distraction is a kind of attention. Law 9: the competent-speaker test fails. If an edge is warranted, DEPENDS_ON would be more apt.

Vernacular is everyday speech of a community, maintained for effective communication within that group. Law 8d: is it built or maintained for the sake of communication? Yes. The servant (vernacular) points at the master (communication).

An initialism is a well-defined linguistic construct: abbreviations formed from initial letters (e.g. FBI, NASA, UNESCO), pronounced letter by letter. Negative space is a structural relation, not limited to visual art. The scope should cover the general pattern of 'space that functions through relation to surrounding elements' across media. Law 4: the carving is too narrow — it would fit many things in visual art but no thing beyond it.

visual-rhetoric IS a specific kind of rhetoric. Rhetoric is the art of persuasion through symbols; visual-rhetoric applies that same persuasive function to visual media. refraction (systematic bending of meaning through interpretive media) does not DEPEND_ON interpretation. tact DEPENDS_ON communication fails the removal test: tact is the concept of social appropriateness, not an operational system needing communication to run. Algorithm design is the activity/practice of designing algorithms, not a methodology. Methodology is the study or analysis of methods (from -logy = study of). Algorithm design is a disciplined practice, a set of procedures, but calling it a 'methodology' misstates its nature. A competent speaker would not describe algorithm design as 'a methodology' — they would call it a practice, discipline, or process. The correct relationship might be INSTANCE_OF (to process, activity, or design-method) but methodology is the wrong general.

Mathematics clearly predates algorithm design. The formal study of algorithms grew from mathematical logic (Turing machines, Church's lambda calculus) and computation theory. Algorithms are mathematical procedures made explicit and executable. Law 7 (DERIVED_FROM): which existed first? Mathematics — yes. Did it feed into algorithm design? Yes, mathematically and historically. The note's reasoning about formal study of algorithms growing directly from mathematical logic and computation theory is correct.

Variation as a property/quality exists independently of the act of comparing it. The concept picks out a real feature of sets — difference within a set — and that picking out operates even without an explicit comparison act. Comparison is a separate concept that helps us detect variation, but variation itself doesn't need comparison to be a concept that operates.

Path-dependence describes a phenomenon where outcomes depend on the sequence of prior events/steps. The note argues it DEPENDS_ON process because 'a process IS a sequence of events/steps.' Path-dependence is a way of DESCRIBING certain processes, not something that requires process as its operating substrate. If anything, path-dependence INSTANCE_OF pattern or phenomenon.
